To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RavA-LdcI complex is a unique cage formed via lateral interactions between the five hexameric rings of RavA, that the LdcI decamer interacts with a single hexamer of RavA via a specific interface, and that this interface is conserved in the LdcI-like proteins of the LdcI family.
we have solved the 3D structures of the RavA–LdcI and LdcI–LdcI binding domains of RavA complexes by cryo-electromicroscopy.

we have determined the structure of a 3.3-MDa macromolecular cage formed by hexamer and decamer proteins, which is unique for the AAA+ ATPase family, and that the structure of the minimal complex of the cage components has been determined to 7.5-Å resolution.

the molecular mechanisms of the assembly of the macromolecular cage formed by hexamer- and decamer-forming Escherichia coliproteins with seemingly incompatible sym-metries.
the molecular mechanisms of protein folding and protein degradation in the bacterial cell, with the goal of understanding the fundamental principles of protein homeostasis and its regulation.
